verdict: Claude path: 104/120 h (86.7%), 61/77 on needs-work lines (79.2%), 1 m, 0 broken, 0 facts or meanings changed. It is safe and close to Typefully on taste, and safer than Typefully on hedges, sarcasm and sensitive lines. It misses 9.5 on three things: the validator rejected 3 good Claude lines (all 3 false positives, one of which shipped a 380-char unchanged fallback), about 15 lines got a one-word trim where a restructure was needed, and 4 whys/receipts are garbled or overclaim. On-device: 84/120 h (70%), 41/77 on needs-work (53.2%), 5 m, 4 broken, 1 statement turned into a question. It never damages a sharp line, but three broken lines ship in the homepage Try box as is. Call marks help on forecasts and personal lines; they misfire on sarcasm and on a repeated-word joke, and cut-versus-call is inconsistent on-device.
to_95: Fix the three validator false positives: a number with a dropped modifier ('over 40 different B2B founders' -> 'over 40 B2B founders'), a shortened age ('43 years old' -> '43'), and 'future lost' on a thread pointer that keeps 'In this thread:'.
When a line over 280 falls back, never ship it still over 280 with its run-up intact; prefer a Claude alt, or the homepage's post-1 cut.
Fix the three on-device grammar breaks: 'vast majority of them' -> 'Most them'; a '?' appended to a statement after a colon; a beat split that eats the 'and' of a list.

Prompt: on lines that lead with a run-up ('Big news!!', 'Why we decided to basically…', 'New issue is out now') pick the restructure, not the one-word trim; don't park the cut announcement at the end ('Very excited to announce it').
Prompt: don't swap one cliché for another ('game changer' -> 'It changes everything'); keep the writer's phrase or cut it.
Whys: stop appending fragments ('“but i really” went too', '“honestly a game” went too'), make the receipt count match the edits, and don't say 'Already sharp' on a line carrying three soft words.

Call marks: no call on sarcasm ('Really groundbreaking') or on a deliberate repeat ('probably. probably.'); one rule for 'probably', 'sort of' and 'I'd argue' so the same word is not cut in one line and a call in the next.
On-device: flag doubled 'that' and stock run-ups ('Here's a little something that I wish that I knew', 'Something that I've noticed is that') instead of 'Nothing to cut'.
Homepage: don't say 'The marked words are your call' when the line shows no call marks.

issues.where: SHARPEN.fromClaude fact/tense checks; k-38, k-55, k-76
issues.problem: 3 of 3 rejects were false positives. k-38 'future lost' shipped a 380-char fallback opening 'In this thread, I am going to break down exactly' in place of two clean sub-280 Claude versions. k-55 called 'over 40 B2B founders' an added fact. k-76 called '43' a lost '43 years old'.
issues.fix: Compare numbers with their head noun after dropping modifiers; treat 'N years old' and 'N' after 'I'm' as the same fact; don't apply the future-tense check when the thread pointer survives.

issues.problem: 'the vast majority of them make' ships as 'Most them make the same mistake.' The plain-word swap drops 'of'. Ships on the homepage.
issues.fix: Map 'the vast majority of' -> 'most of' before a pronoun, 'most' before a noun; add 'most them/us/you' to the broken patterns.

issues.problem: A statement became a question: 'Anyone using Postgres: you probably don't actually need Redis for your job queue?' The line now opens on 'Anyone' and gets a '?'. Ships on the homepage.
issues.fix: Only add '?' when the main clause is interrogative; 'Anyone …:' followed by a declarative clause is an address, not a question.

issues.problem: 'supports plugins, config files, and it's also…' ships as 'supports plugins, config files. It's also…': the split takes the list's 'and'.
issues.fix: Don't split at ', and' when the text before it is an unclosed comma list; or restore 'and' before the last item.

issues.problem: The 390-char line ships as a 'How we…' fragment welded to 'and I'm also going to share…', ending in a colon. The homepage shows a cleaner post-1 cut, so the two paths disagree.
issues.fix: Use the homepage's first-sentence cut in core too, or keep the line as written with the over-280 note.

issues.where: prompts.sharpen; k-27, k-30, k-42, k-48, k-78, k-79, k-80, k-92
issues.problem: About 15 lines are better but soft: one-word trims on lines that needed a restructure, 'Very excited to announce it' parked after the news, a 'Why…' fragment with a full stop, and 'game changer' swapped for 'It changes everything'.
issues.fix: Tell the prompt to prefer the version that opens on the news or number when the draft opens on a run-up, to drop (not move) announce-the-announcement phrases, and never to trade one stock phrase for another.

issues.where: fromClaude why/say assembly; k-20, k-92, k-89, k-5
issues.problem: Whys end on appended fragments ('“but i really” went too', '“honestly a game” went too'); k-92's receipt says 5 cuts; k-89 says three beats; k-5 says 'Already sharp' on an unchanged line with three soft words.
issues.fix: Drop the auto-appended 'went too' when it overlaps a phrase the why already names; count receipts from the final diff; reserve 'Already sharp' for lines with no flagged words.

issues.where: slCallMarks; k-61, k-24, k-41, k-17, k-91
issues.problem: Sarcastic 'Really groundbreaking' is marked 'A hype word'; both halves of 'probably. probably.' are marked; on-device cuts 'probably' in k-41 and 'sort of' in k-17 outright but offers the same words as calls elsewhere.
issues.fix: Skip call marks inside lines the engine already recognises as sarcasm or deliberate repetition; decide cut-vs-call by word class, not by line.

issues.problem: 'Here's a little something that I wish that I knew' returns 'Nothing to cut' with no marks; run-ups like 'Something that I've noticed is that' and 'A quick little thread on the reasons why I think' survive.
issues.fix: Add these run-ups and the doubled 'that' to the throat-clearing patterns.

issues.problem: Homepage output differs from core on 2 of 15 lines, and on k-92 it says 'The marked words are your call' with no call marks shown.
issues.fix: Use KEPT_WHY only when a call mark is rendered; otherwise the plain 'nothing it could cut safely' text.
